mainTopic: Following רבי שמעון on מוקצה and its limits, then the משנה on dissolving vows on שבת: whether a שבת need is required, the time window for הפרה, and the story of the sealed window.
overview: The amud opens by testing רבי יוחנן, who rules like רבי שמעון's lenient view of מוקצה because he follows a סתם משנה. Three unattributed משניות seem to follow the strict רבי יהודה. The first is assigned to רבי יוסי בר יהודה. The second is explained as מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, which even רבי שמעון forbids. For the third, the גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן relied on a weightier source: בית הלל, as reversed by רב נחמן, follows רבי שמעון. רב אחא and רבינא then argue over which kinds of מוקצה are exceptions to following רבי שמעון. Both agree that מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס is forbidden, and this is proven from the large saw and the plow blade. A new משנה then permits הפרת נדרים and asking a חכם about vows on שבת, along with sealing, measuring, and tying. The גמרא asks whether the limit 'for the needs of שבת' applies to הפרה too. It connects this question to the תנאים's dispute over whether הפרה lasts כל היום or מעת לעת, and it rules that a חכם may dissolve a vow on שבת even if the person had time before. Finally, רב begins explaining the משנה's story of the sealed window, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An unattributed משנה that seems to follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a סתם משנה forbidding chopping firewood from building beams or from a beam that broke on יום טוב. This looks like רבי יהודה's strict view of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not chop firewood from beams, and not from a beam that broke on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with an unnamed משנה. This משנה treats a beam that broke on יום טוב as forbidden, which matches רבי יהודה's strict approach to מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן rules like an unattributed משנה, and he holds like רבי שמעון. A beam that broke on יום טוב was not ready for burning when the day began. Forbidding it fits רבי יהודה's concept of מוקצה, so it seems a סתם משנה follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: chopping (wood)
beams set aside for building
broke
an item set aside and not to be moved or used on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: One may not chop wood from the beams,
phrases.notes: Beams are set aside for building, not for burning.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: nor from a beam that broke on a Festival.
phrases.notes: It was not fit for burning when the day started.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier series of challenges against רבי יוחנן from unattributed משניות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון because a סתם משנה follows him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unattributed משנה forbids a beam that broke on יום טוב, which reflects רבי יהודה's view of מוקצה. If רבי יוחנן always follows a סתם משנה, he should rule like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן assigns that משנה to רבי יוסי בר יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he learns this משנה as the individual view of רבי יוסי בר יהודה. It is therefore not a true unattributed ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: that משנה, I teach it according to רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that this משנה is really the opinion of one specific תנא, רבי יוסי בר יהודה. So it does not carry the authority of a סתם משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following a סתם משנה only works when the משנה is truly anonymous. Once רבי יוחנן attributes this משנה to a single named authority, it becomes an individual opinion. It therefore cannot force the הלכה to follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא whose individual view this משנה reflects
he teaches it (attributes the teaching to)
that one

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan: that one —

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה מַתְנֵי לַהּ.
phrases.english: he teaches it according to Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.
phrases.notes: It is an individual opinion, not a true סתם משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, הָהוּא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה מַתְנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution: the anonymous משנה is assigned to an individual תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is an anonymous ruling that follows רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is the individual opinion of רבי יוסי בר יהודה, so it does not bind רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Challenge from starting a fire with straw but not stored wood
steps.stepSummary: Another סתם משנה allows lighting a fire with a pile of straw but not with wood from the storage area. This again seems to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may start a fire with a pile of straw, but not with wood that is in the storage area!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second unattributed משנה that seems to follow רבי יהודה. It forbids using stored wood as מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood in the storage area behind the house was put away for other purposes. Forbidding it looks like the strict מוקצה view of רבי יהודה. So the challenge to רבי יוחנן returns.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source)
one may start (a fire)
a pile of straw

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One may start a fire with a pile of straw,
but not with the wood that is in the storage area!
phrases.notes: Here מוקצה refers to the storage area behind the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unattributed משנה forbids stored wood as מוקצה, which seems to reflect רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Expensive cedar and fir wood is a case even רבי שמעון forbids
steps.stepSummary: The stored wood is costly cedar and fir. It is מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, which even רבי שמעון agrees is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is talking about cedar and fir wood, which is מוקצה because of monetary loss, and in that case even רבי שמעון agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this משנה deals with a special kind of מוקצה. Both sides forbid it, so the משנה does not prove anything about רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cedar and fir are valuable building woods, and the owner would never want them burned. Items set aside out of fear of financial loss are forbidden even according to the lenient רבי שמעון. So this משנה fits רבי שמעון's view as well.

keyTerms.meaning: cedars and firs (valuable woods)
set aside because of fear of monetary loss
agrees

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key category: מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס is forbidden by everyone. The end of this passage proves it from a משנה.

phrases.english: There it is referring to cedars and firs,
which are set aside due to monetary loss,
and even Rabbi Shimon concedes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה deals with a category on which everyone agrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids stored wood because of רבי יהודה's general view of מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals with valuable wood that is מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס, which even רבי שמעון forbids.

steps.title: Challenge from desert animals versus household animals
steps.stepSummary: A third סתם משנה forbids watering and slaughtering wild-grazing animals on יום טוב but permits household animals. This again seems to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may not water and slaughter desert animals, but one may water and slaughter household animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third unattributed משנה that treats animals grazing out in the wilderness as מוקצה. This seems to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals that live out in the fields were not set aside for use on יום טוב, so they are treated as מוקצה. Household animals are ready for use, so they are allowed. This is another סתם משנה that seems to follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: give water to (animals)
slaughter
desert animals that graze outside all year
household animals that sleep in town

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One may not water and slaughter desert animals,
but one may water and slaughter household animals!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין מַשְׁקִין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַמִּדְבָּרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge of the same type.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another unattributed משנה applies מוקצה strictly, in line with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן relied on a different unattributed משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן found another סתם משנה that follows רבי שמעון: the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל about clearing bones and peels from the table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found a different anonymous משנה. בית שמאי say: one may lift bones and peels off the table. בית הלל say: one removes the whole board and shakes it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer the desert-animal משנה directly. Instead it explains that רבי יוחנן relied on a different משנה that, in his view, carries more weight and follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When unattributed משניות conflict, רבי יוחנן had to choose one. He chose a ruling of בית הלל, since the הלכה always follows בית הלל, and such a ruling counts like a סתם משנה. As written here, though, בית הלל sounds strict, so step 7 is needed to complete the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: a different unattributed (משנה)
he found
bones and peels (food scraps, normally מוקצה)
board or tray on top of the table
shakes it off

steps.confusionAlert: As written in this משנה, בית הלל seem to be the strict ones, since they forbid lifting the scraps directly. Don't stop here. רב נחמן in the next step reverses the opinions, and only then does בית הלל follow רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan found a different unattributed Mishnah:
Beit Shammai say:
One may lift bones and peels off the table,
and Beit Hillel say:
One removes the entire board and shakes it off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 5, and to the whole series, by pointing to a competing source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Competing source: רבי יוחנן relied on another unattributed משנה that outweighs the others.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule of following the סתם משנה would force him to rule like רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן relied on a different, weightier source that follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב נחמן reverses the opinions so בית הלל follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן teaches that the opinions should be reversed. בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה and בית הלל follow רבי שמעון, so the binding view of בית הלל supports רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: we have it only as בית שמאי following רבי יהודה, and בית הלל following רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן switches the two positions in the בית שמאי and בית הלל dispute. This makes בית הלל the lenient ones, matching רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the reversal, בית הלל allow lifting the bones and peels directly, just as רבי שמעון is lenient about מוקצה. Since the הלכה always follows בית הלל, this ruling works like a סתם משנה in favor of רבי שמעון. This is what completes רבי יוחנן's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who reverses the positions
we have (the text) only as

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said,
we have it only as
Beit Shammai in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
and Beit Hillel in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 6 by showing that the cited משנה actually supports רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן had a binding source for ruling like רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of בית הלל, as reversed by רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי שמעון on מוקצה. His source is בית הלל, as reversed by רב נחמן, which carries the weight of a סתם משנה.

steps.title: First view: follow רבי שמעון except for repulsive items like an old lamp
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in all of הלכות שבת, except for מוקצה מחמת מיאוס, such as an old lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One said: in all of שבת the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, except for מוקצה because of repulsiveness. What is that? An old lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens about the limits of ruling like רבי שמעון. The first opinion makes one exception: items that are disgusting, like a dirty old oil lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון generally allows moving items that are not actively forbidden. This opinion agrees, except that items people avoid because they are repulsive stay forbidden. A used, grimy oil lamp is the classic example.

keyTerms.meaning: they disagree
two אמוראים in the disagreement
set aside because it is repulsive
an old (dirty) oil lamp
except for

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagree about this,
one said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלָּהּ הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: in all of Shabbat, the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,
except for an item set aside due to repulsiveness,
and what is that? An old lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, the גמרא now defines that rule's exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון throughout הלכות שבת, except for מוקצה מחמת מיאוס, such as an old lamp.

steps.title: Second view: follow רבי שמעון even for repulsive items, except a lamp lit that שבת
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion holds that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון even for repulsive items. The only exception is מוקצה מחמת איסור, a lamp that was burning on that same שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: for מוקצה because of repulsiveness, the הלכה also follows רבי שמעון, except for מוקצה because of a prohibition. What is that? A lamp that was lit on that same שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion is even more lenient. Only an item tied to a forbidden act, like a lamp that was lit during this שבת, remains forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the old, dirty lamp may be moved. The one exception is a lamp that was burning when שבת began. It was set aside because of a forbidden act, since it was being used for a flame on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: also
set aside because of a prohibition
a lamp that was lit on that same שבת

phrases.english: And one said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוּקְצֶה מֵחֲמַת מִיאוּס נָמֵי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: with an item set aside due to repulsiveness too, the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,
except for an item set aside due to prohibition,
and what is that?
A lamp that was lit on that same Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: בְּמוּקְצֶה מֵחֲמַת מִיאוּס נָמֵי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view in the same disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון even for מוקצה מחמת מיאוס. Only מוקצה מחמת איסור, such as a lamp lit on that שבת, is forbidden.

steps.title: Items guarded against monetary loss are forbidden even for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס is forbidden even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with מוקצה because of monetary loss, even רבי שמעון agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes a category that is never part of the leniency. Everyone, including רבי שמעון, forbids moving items the owner protects from damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side's list of exceptions applies here, because this category was never included in רבי שמעון's leniency in the first place. When an owner purposely keeps an item from any casual use, he has clearly set it aside. This ties back to the cedar and fir answer in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: but

phrases.english: But an item set aside due to monetary loss,
even Rabbi Shimon concedes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מוּקְצֶה מֵחֲמַת חֶסְרוֹן כִּיס, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a category that is forbidden in all opinions, alongside the exceptions just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס is forbidden even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה of the large saw and plow blade
steps.stepSummary: The proof is a משנה: all vessels may be moved on שבת except a large saw and a plow blade, which are guarded against damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: all vessels may be moved on שבת, except for a large saw and the blade of a plow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the previous step from a משנה that follows רבי שמעון. That משנה still forbids valuable tools the owner is careful not to damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה is lenient, allowing all vessels, which shows it follows רבי שמעון. Even so, it excludes a large saw and a plow blade, because owners keep them for their special job only. So even רבי שמעון forbids מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
may be moved
a large saw
the blade or peg of a plow

steps.whatToRemember: There are three kinds of מוקצה. מיאוס (repulsive) and איסור (forbidden) are disputed by רב אחא and רבינא. חסרון כיס (fear of monetary loss) is forbidden by everyone, even רבי שמעון, as proven from the large saw and plow blade.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
All vessels may be moved on Shabbat,
except for a large saw
and the blade of a plow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That even רבי שמעון forbids מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: all vessels may be moved on שבת except a large saw and a plow blade.

steps.title: The משנה lists what may be done on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits הפרת נדרים on שבת, asking a חכם to dissolve vows needed for שבת, sealing a window, and measuring a rag or a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A husband or father may cancel vows on שבת. One may also ask a חכם to undo vows that are needed for שבת. One may block up a window, measure a rag, and measure a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It lists several actions that are allowed on שבת even though they look like weekday business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different ways to remove a vow. הפרה is done by a husband or father, and התרה (שאלה) is done by asking a חכם. The phrase 'for the needs of שבת' is clearly attached to asking a חכם, and the גמרא will soon ask whether it also applies to הפרה. Measuring a rag (to see if it is big enough to become טמא) and measuring a מקוה (to see if it has enough water) are permitted because they are done for a מצוה purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling vows. A husband or father can do this for his wife's or daughter's vows.
Asking a חכם to dissolve one's own vow.
Blocking up a window or light-opening.
A rag. It must be a minimum size to become טמא.
A ritual bath. It needs a minimum amount of water.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse הפרה (a husband or father cancels a woman's vow by himself) with שאלה/התרה (a person asks a חכם to undo his own vow). They are two separate mechanisms.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may nullify vows on Shabbat,
and one may request (from a Sage) to dissolve vows
that are for the purpose of Shabbat.
And one may seal a window,
and one may measure a rag,
and one may measure a ritual bath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It begins a new topic after the מוקצה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may do הפרת נדרים, dissolve vows through a חכם when they are needed for שבת, seal a window, and measure a rag or a מקוה.

steps.title: A historical story supports sealing, measuring, and tying
steps.stepSummary: In the days of רבי צדוק's father and אבא שאול בן בטנית, people sealed a window with a jug and tied a shard to a reed to measure an opening. This shows that sealing, measuring, and tying are allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story in the days of רבי צדוק's father and אבא שאול בן בטנית. They blocked a window with a clay jug. They also tied a clay shard to a reed to check whether a roof covering had an opening of a טפח. From what they did, we learn that one may seal, measure, and tie on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real-life story as proof for the rules it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טפח-wide opening matters for טומאת אוהל, because it can let טומאה pass through. So they had to know the size of the opening. Blocking the window, measuring with the reed, and tying a temporary knot were all done on שבת. This proves that each of those actions is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An earthenware jug or vessel.
A clay shard or piece of a broken vessel.
A reed or rush, used here as a measuring stick.
A roof covering or overhang.
An opening one handbreadth wide. This is the size that matters for טומאה.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's permission to seal, measure, and tie on שבת is backed by an actual practice of earlier חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בִּימֵי אָבִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי צָדוֹק
phrases.english: And there was an incident in the days of Rabbi Tzadok's father
and in the days of Abba Shaul ben Botnit
that they sealed a window with an earthenware jug,
and tied a clay shard with a reed
to know whether the roof covering had
an opening of a handbreadth or not,
and from their words we learned
that one may seal, measure, and tie on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בִּימֵי אָבִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rules of step 12 with a story (מעשה).
steps.raayaObject: That sealing, measuring, and tying are permitted on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice in the days of רבי צדוק's father and אבא שאול בן בטנית.

steps.title: Does the limit 'for שבת needs' apply only to asking a חכם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises an איבעיא. First possibility: הפרה is allowed even when not needed for שבת, and only שאלה is limited to שבת needs. That would explain why the משנה lists the two separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked. Maybe cancelling vows is allowed both when it is needed for שבת and when it is not, while asking a חכם is allowed only when needed for שבת and not otherwise. That would be why the משנה separated the two cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a question about how to read the משנה. This step gives the first side; the next line will give the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה wrote 'for the needs of שבת' after the case of asking a חכם, and it listed הפרה separately. One reading says the separation shows that the limit applies only to asking a חכם, so הפרה is allowed for any reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים).
Cancellation of a vow by a husband or father.
Asking a חכם to dissolve a vow.
For the need of (שבת).
He separated them from each other.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: הֲפָרָה בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ,
phrases.english: Is nullification permitted both for the need (of Shabbat) and not for the need,
while a request (to a Sage) for the need: yes,
not for the need: no?
And because of this he separated them from each other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the first clause of the משנה in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the limit 'for the needs of שבת' applies only to שאלה, or also to הפרה.

steps.title: Second side: both require a שבת need
steps.stepSummary: Second possibility: הפרה is also limited to שבת needs. The משנה separated the cases only because הפרה needs no בית דין, while שאלה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps cancelling vows is also allowed only when needed for שבת and not otherwise. The reason the משנה separated them is that cancelling does not need a court, but asking to dissolve a vow does need a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This side offers a different reason for why the משנה separated the two cases. The separation does not show a difference in the שבת rule. It reflects a technical difference: a husband or father does הפרה alone, while התרה requires a חכם or בית דין. If so, both are allowed only for שבת needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. It introduces the second side of a question.
A court. Here, a חכם or panel needed to dissolve vows.
Separates or divides.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
nullification also, for the need: yes,
not for the need: no,
and the fact that he separated them from each other

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲפָרָה אֵין צָרִיךְ בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: is because nullification does not require a court,
while a request requires a court?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the איבעיא by giving the opposite reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's separation of the cases reflects only the need for a בית דין, so that both require a שבת need.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows nullification also requires a שבת need
steps.stepSummary: זוטי of the school of רב פפי taught that one may do הפרת נדרים on שבת for the needs of שבת. This implies that without a שבת need, it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: זוטי of the school of רב פפי taught that one may cancel vows on שבת for the needs of שבת. This implies: for the needs of שבת, yes; not for the needs of שבת, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. It supports the second side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא attaches 'for the needs of שבת' directly to הפרה. From this wording we infer that הפרה without a שבת need is forbidden. So the משנה's separation must be because of the בית דין difference, not a difference in the שבת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. It introduces a source brought as proof.
Taught (a ברייתא).
זוטי, a teacher from the school of רב פפי.

steps.whatToRemember: Even הפרת נדרים is permitted on שבת only when it is needed for שבת. The משנה lists it separately only because it needs no בית דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: no form of removing a vow is done on שבת unless it serves a שבת need.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי [רַב] זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפִּי:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Zutei of the school of Rav Pappa taught:
One may nullify vows on Shabbat
for the purpose of Shabbat.
For the purpose of Shabbat: yes,
not for the purpose of Shabbat: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי [רַב] זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the איבעיא of steps 14 and 15 in favor of the second side.
steps.raayaObject: That הפרה on שבת is also limited to שבת needs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of זוטי of the school of רב פפי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both הפרה and שאלה are permitted only for the needs of שבת.

steps.title: Second version of the question: does 'for the need' cover both, meaning the window is twenty-four hours?
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the first side of the איבעיא says 'for the need' applies to both הפרה and שאלה. That would mean הפרה is valid for a full twenty-four hours (מעת לעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: they asked: Is 'for the need' taught about both of them, so that without a need it is not allowed? If so, it seems that nullifying vows works for a full twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restarts the same question in a new way. It now links the question to how long a husband or father has to cancel a vow. This step gives the first side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הפרה lasts twenty-four hours (מעת לעת), a husband who hears a vow on שבת can simply wait until after שבת. So there is no reason to let him do it on שבת unless he needs it for שבת. That explains why 'for the need' would apply to הפרה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version (of the same discussion)
On both of them
Apparently / this shows that
A full twenty-four-hour period from the time he heard the vow

steps.confusionAlert: In this version, the time window is the REASON behind the שבת rule. A longer window (מעת לעת) leads to a stricter שבת rule: הפרה is allowed only for a שבת need, because he can wait until after שבת.

phrases.english: Another version: they asked:
Is 'for the need' taught about both of them,
so that when it is not for the need, no (not allowed)?
If so, apparently nullification of vows lasts for twenty-four hours,
phrases.notes: He can wait until after שבת, so he does it on שבת only if it is needed for שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the איבעיא of steps 14-15 in a second version. This version connects it to the time window for הפרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'for the need of שבת' also limit הפרה? If so, it would follow that הפרה lasts מעת לעת.

steps.title: Or does 'for the need' apply only to asking a sage, meaning the window ends with the day?
steps.stepSummary: The second side: 'for the need' refers only to שאלה. הפרה is allowed even without a שבת need, because הפרה only lasts until the end of the day (כל היום).
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps when it teaches 'for the need,' it teaches that only about asking a sage. But nullifying vows is allowed even when not needed, which shows that nullifying vows lasts only for that whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question. Maybe the limit 'for the need' is only about asking a חכם, not about הפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הפרה only works until nightfall of the day he heard the vow (כל היום), then a vow heard on שבת must be cancelled on שבת or the chance is lost forever. So the חכמים would allow הפרה on שבת even without any שבת need.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
Asking a חכם to dissolve one's own vow
Only until the end of the day on which he heard the vow

phrases.english: Or perhaps, when it teaches 'for the need' —
it is about asking a sage that it teaches this,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֲפָרַת נְדָרִים אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ,
phrases.english: but nullification of vows is allowed even when not for the need,
which shows that nullification of vows lasts only for the whole day.
phrases.notes: If he waits until after שבת, the window has closed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the איבעיא opened in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the limit 'for the need' only on שאלה? If so, it would follow that הפרה lasts only כל היום.

steps.title: רב זוטי's ברייתא shows the window is twenty-four hours
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רב זוטי says הפרה on שבת is only for שבת needs. In this version, that means הפרה lasts מעת לעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב זוטי of the school of רב פפי taught: One may nullify vows on שבת for the needs of שבת. For the needs of שבת, yes. Not for the needs of שבת, no. This shows that nullifying vows lasts twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same ברייתא as in the first version. This time it uses it to settle the question about the time window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits הפרה itself to שבת needs. So in this version, the reason must be that he can wait until after שבת. That means הפרה lasts מעת לעת.

keyTerms.meaning: One may nullify (a husband or father cancelling a vow)
Yes
No

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפִּי:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for רב זוטי of the school of רב פפי taught:
One may nullify vows on שבת for the needs of שבת.
For the needs of שבת — yes,
not for the needs of שבת — no,
which shows that nullification of vows lasts twenty-four hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second-version איבעיא. It repeats the ברייתא from step 16 for a new purpose: proving מעת לעת.
steps.raayaObject: That הפרה is limited to שבת needs, and therefore that הפרה lasts מעת לעת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב זוטי דבי רב פפי.

steps.title: רב אשי objects: a משנה says the window is only the whole day
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the conclusion from a משנה that clearly says הפרה lasts כל היום, with both leniencies and stringencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: But we learned in a משנה: Nullifying vows lasts the whole day, and this can make things easier or stricter. How? If she vowed on Friday night, he may nullify on Friday night and all of שבת day until dark. If she vowed just before dark, he may nullify only until dark. If he did not nullify before dark, he can no longer nullify.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the conclusion of step 19 (מעת לעת). He quotes a משנה that clearly says the window is only until the day ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the window depends on the calendar day, not on twenty-four hours. A vow made on Friday night gives him almost a full day, which is the leniency. A vow made just before dark gives him only minutes, which is the stringency. That contradicts the conclusion that הפרה lasts מעת לעת.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned (in a משנה)! (introduces a contradiction)
To be lenient and to be strict
Right at nightfall
Until it gets dark

phrases.english: רב אשי said: But we learned in a משנה:
Nullification of vows lasts the whole day,
and this matter can work out both leniently and strictly.
How so? If she vowed on Friday night —

phrases.aramaic: מֵיפֵר לֵילֵי שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת עַד שֶׁתֶּחְשַׁךְ.
phrases.english: he may nullify on Friday night and on שבת day until it gets dark.
phrases.notes: This is the leniency: almost a full day.

phrases.english: If she vowed right at nightfall —
he may nullify only until it gets dark,
phrases.notes: This is the stringency: only a few minutes.

phrases.english: for if he did not nullify by the time it got dark,
he can no longer nullify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 19 that הפרה lasts מעת לעת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that הפרת נדרים lasts מעת לעת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly says הפרה lasts כל היום and gives examples where the window ends at nightfall. That contradicts מעת לעת.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the length of the window is a dispute among תנאים. The ברייתא of רב זוטי follows the view of מעת לעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it was taught: Nullifying vows lasts the whole day. רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said: twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי's challenge. It shows that there are two opinions among the תנאים about how long the window lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that רב אשי quoted follows the view of כל היום. The ברייתא of רב זוטי follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who hold מעת לעת. So the two sources do not contradict; they reflect different opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
A תנא who holds the window is twenty-four hours
A תנא who agrees with רבי יוסי בר יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: How long the window for הפרה lasts is a dispute among תנאים: כל היום (the end of the day) versus מעת לעת (twenty-four hours). In the second version, this dispute decides whether הפרה on שבת needs a שבת purpose.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it was taught:
Nullification of vows lasts the whole day.
רבי יוסי בר יהודה
and רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון said:
Twenty-four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: the two sources follow different opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה of כל היום seemed to be the only view, which would contradict the ברייתא of רב זוטי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא of רב זוטי follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who hold מעת לעת.

steps.title: Asking a sage on שבת: only if there was no time before?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה, asking a חכם to dissolve vows on שבת. It asks whether this is allowed only when there was no time before שבת, or even when there was time.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may ask a sage about vows.' They asked: Is this only when he did not have time before שבת, or perhaps even when he did have time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new question about the next part of the משנה. It wants to know if asking a חכם on שבת is allowed even for someone who could have done it earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שאלה is allowed only for שבת needs, one might think it is also limited to someone who had no other chance. The other possibility is that any שבת need is enough, even if he could have asked before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One may ask a חכם to dissolve vows
Free time / opportunity
They asked (an open question for the בית המדרש)

phrases.english: 'And one may ask a sage about vows.' They asked:
Is it only when he did not have time before שבת,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אֲפִילּוּ הָיָה לוֹ פְּנַאי?
phrases.english: or perhaps even when he did have time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הפרה discussion and quotes the next phrase of the משנה from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is שאלה on שבת allowed only when the person had no time to ask before שבת, or even when he had time?

steps.title: The sages dissolved רב זוטרא's vow even though he had time
steps.stepSummary: A story proves that a חכם may dissolve a vow on שבת even when the person had time to ask before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The rabbis attended to רב זוטרא son of רב זירא and dissolved his vow, even though he had time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a real case. The חכמים dissolved רב זוטרא's vow on שבת even though he could have asked before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים acted even though he had time earlier, so having had time does not block שאלה on שבת. As long as the vow is needed for שבת, a חכם may dissolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: They attended to / took up his case
They permitted (dissolved)
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: Asking a חכם to dissolve a vow on שבת (for a שבת need) is allowed even if the person had time to ask before שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear: the rabbis attended to
רב זוטרא, son of רב זירא,
and dissolved his vow for him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ פְּנַאי.
phrases.english: even though he had had time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the איבעיא of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That שאלה on שבת is allowed even when the person had time before שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case: the חכמים dissolved רב זוטרא בריה דרב זירא's vow on שבת.

steps.title: Quoting the story of the sealed window from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: they sealed a window with a pitcher and tied a pot shard with a reed. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: they sealed the window with a pitcher and tied the pot shard with a reed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so that it can explain it. This is a setup step that prepares for רב's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was explaining the line about dissolving vows on שבת. Now it turns to the final story in the משנה. That story describes people on שבת using household objects (a pitcher and a pot shard) for a purpose connected to טומאה. The גמרא first quotes it and then explains what the case was.

keyTerms.meaning: They plugged or sealed (an opening)
A window or opening that lets in light
An earthenware pitcher or jug
An earthenware pot or a shard of one
Reed-grass, a soft plant used like a rope

phrases.english: That they sealed the window with an earthenware pitcher
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the words of the משנה.

phrases.english: and tied the earthenware pot shard with reed-grass.
phrases.notes: A soft reed was used to tie it, not a regular rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the line about dissolving vows on שבת to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotation of the משנה phrase to be explained: sealing a window with a pitcher and tying a pot shard with reed.

steps.title: רב explains the setting: a small alley with טומאת מת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, begins explaining the story: there was a small alley between two houses, and there was טומאה in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: there was a small alley between two houses, and there was טומאה there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב begins to describe the real-life situation behind the משנה's story. He starts with the setting: a narrow alley between two houses that contained טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only tells us what the people did. רב supplies the background so we can understand why they did it. The טומאה was טומאת מת, which can spread through roofed areas and openings. That explains why it mattered whether a window was sealed or how big an opening was. His explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A small, narrow alleyway or passage
Ritual impurity; here, impurity from a dead body
Houses

steps.confusionAlert: The story is not about the window or pot on their own. Everything they did was to deal with the טומאה in the alley. Keep that background in mind as רב's explanation continues.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
There was a small alleyway
between two houses,
and there was ritual impurity there
phrases.notes: Impurity from a corpse, which can spread through roofed spaces and openings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הִילְקָטִי קְטַנָּה הָיְתָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי בָתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the משנה phrase quoted in the previous step by describing the actual case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's story took place in a small alley between two houses where there was טומאה. The explanation continues on the next amud.
